name: USPD StabilizerNFT unprotected initializer on a freshly deployed proxy
summary: The StabilizerNFT ERC-1967 proxy was deployed without running its unprotected initialize(). Twelve seconds later the attacker called it, took the admin and upgrader roles and hid them behind a swapped-back implementation; 79 days later it upgraded the proxy to mint unbacked USPD, drained stETH from escrows and sold USPD for the pool's USDC.
notes: The proxy’s first Upgraded event, log 524 of its own creation transaction, selected the audited implementation 0x11a880b0c9d50b4aef7527d458497e60fa602429. That implementation is still selected when the anchor transaction delegate-calls its initialize() twelve seconds later.

Campaign: the drain 0xa7cab072, two later re-mints through the hijacked proxy, and eight sales of unbacked USPD/cUSPD into the USPD/USDC pool. Loss is the stETH taken from position and stabilizer escrows plus all USDC the pool lost; unbacked USPD, LP tokens and the repaid Balancer flash loan are excluded.
Anchor is the clandestine initialization 12 s after deployment (rule 12); the same actor later front-ran the proxy's initialization on Arbitrum and Polygon, but no assets left on those chains.
